clue.text: Break point with return I fancy

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or ornamental, so these letters are worked into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A tennis player at break point hopes their return will be good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break point' reads as one tennis phrase; in fact 'Break' is the definition and POINT, RETURN and I are shuffled together, signalled by 'fancy'.
explanation.definitionFit: A break in proceedings is a pause or stoppage, a synonym for an interruption.

clue.text: Quite miserable penning record

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as a pen holds sheep, so the two words hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: Someone thoroughly fed up while writing down a record of events.
explanation.definitionFit: To record things one by one, setting out each detail in a list, is to itemize them.

clue.text: Managed walk round ends of terrace

indicators.note: round says the walking word goes around the other letters

parts.note: to tread is to walk

indicators.note: ends of takes the first and last letters of the word terrace

explanation.surface: Someone managed to stroll around the edge of a patio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Managed' could be the past tense of handling a person or a problem; here it means dealt with, as in treated a topic.
explanation.definitionFit: To have treated a matter is to have dealt with or handled it, so managed is a synonym.

clue.text: Control balance, with drops over time

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the earlier piece above the later one

parts.note: the balance or remainder is the rest
raindrops: drops can mean rain

explanation.surface: Keeping balance while dripping water steadily over time sounds like a lab experiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint is self-control or the act of holding something in check.

clue.text: Open a French champagne and party starts

parts.note: un is the French word for a

indicators.note: starts asks for the opening letters of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: Pop open a bottle of French champagne and the party gets going.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncap a bottle is to take its top off, which opens it.

clue.text: Couple with wife very large in volume

indicators.note: in places the wife and size letters inside the book word

parts.note: a volume or large book is a tome
OS stands for outsize, very large in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A pair with a hugely heavy wife sounds like an unkind sketch.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple is a pair of people, and a pair is a twosome.

clue.text: Abundant work university provided

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
lent means provided on loan

explanation.surface: Plenty of work arrives at a university that someone has supplied.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent means rich and plentiful, so abundant is a near synonym.

clue.text: Badly ruins ground on small habitat

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are put together wrongly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Damage that ruins the soil spoils a small creature's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link placing the small letter after the shuffled pair, in an across-style reading of the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the environment where something lives, its surroundings.

clue.text: Poor American English the French start to speak

parts.note: les is the French plural for the

indicators.note: start to points to the opening letter of the word speak

explanation.surface: An American's poor English when the French people begin talking.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor, as in poor work, means of little worth or effectiveness.

clue.text: Cold look facing certain bankruptcy

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
lo is an old word for look
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A frosty gaze from a businessman facing sure ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: A business going bust ends in a shutdown, so bankruptcy brings its end.

clue.text: Tricky compiler's given up, except for trapping idiot

indicators.note: given up in a down clue means written upwards, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: the compiler is the setter, who refers to themselves as me; the 's stands for is

indicators.note: trapping says the idiot word is caught inside the other

parts.note: barring means except for
an ass is an idiot

explanation.surface: A setter has given up, except for trapping one fool: an awkward confession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compiler's' is read 'compiler is': ME turned upwards gives EM.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricky or awkward situation can be embarrassing, causing discomfort.

clue.text: Part of hero is terrific romp

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A film blurb praising a hero's performance in a fun romp.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to revel noisily, much as to romp is to play boisterously.

clue.text: Saw voting system finished British

parts.note: PR is proportional representation, a voting system
over means finished

explanation.surface: Someone saw that the British voting system had come to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a verb but is the noun: an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying, a traditional maxim of folk wisdom.

clue.text: Turn over page covered by nude spread

indicators.note: covered by says the page letter sits inside the other letters
spread suggests the letters are scattered and laid out anew

explanation.surface: Flipping the page of a magazine to find a nude spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' turns NUDE into UEND, which wraps P.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend something is to turn it upside down, to overturn it.

clue.text: One script rewritten for 'Morse', perhaps …

indicators.note: a script rewritten has its words reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A screenplay revised for the TV detective drama Morse.
explanation.walkthrough: Morse is the fictional Oxford police detective of novels and long-running British TV.
explanation.definitionFit: Morse holds the police rank of detective chief inspector, so he is one example.

clue.text: Worker day after day before in hold

indicators.note: in sets those letters inside the hold word

parts.note: to hold is to store

indicators.note: after places the day abbreviation following the day-before word

parts.note: eve is the day before an occasion

explanation.surface: A dockhand working day after day in a ship's hold.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore is a dock labourer who loads and unloads ships.

clue.text: … separate detective's partner talked oddly

parts.note: DI is a detective inspector, plus the S of the possessive
a man can be a partner, as in man and wife

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of the word talked

explanation.surface: Continuing the Morse clue: his sidekick spoke strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to the Morse clue; Morse's partner was Lewis.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle is to take apart, separating something into its pieces.

clue.text: Singer thus performed opera's intro around piano

indicators.note: around says those letters go round the piano letter

parts.note: so means thus
ran, as in ran a show, means performed

indicators.note: intro asks for the opening letter of opera

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A singer performs the opening of an opera beside a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano is a singer with the highest voice range.

clue.text: Ally could be one of enemy

definitions.text: Ally could be one of enemy

parts.words: Ally could be one of enemy
parts.note: ally and enemy are opposite words, so ally is an example of the opposite of enemy

explanation.surface: A warning that a friend could turn out to be a foe.
explanation.definitionFit: A word of opposite meaning to another, as ally is to enemy.

clue.text: 'Mob' arousing fear in America initially

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letters of each of the five preceding words

explanation.surface: Organised criminals terrorised America at first.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds the answer from its initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mob is the organised crime syndicate that first terrified American cities.

clue.text: Noble fellow pockets silver coin finally

indicators.note: pockets says the fellow word holds the other letters

parts.note: a mate is a fellow or companion
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: finally asks for the last letter of coin

explanation.surface: An aristocrat's friend slips a silver coin into his pocket at last.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnate is a great or powerful person, historically a nobleman of high rank.

clue.text: Stocks trader?

parts.note: stocks are also garden flowers, so a seller of them is a flower seller rather than a stockbroker

explanation.walkthrough: Stocks look like shares; here they are the scented flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop selling cut flowers and plants deals in blooms such as stocks.

clue.text: Relatively helpful?

parts.note: relatively here means towards relatives, describing favouritism shown to family

explanation.walkthrough: 'Relatively' seems to mean somewhat; read it as 'to relatives'.
explanation.definitionFit: Favouring relatives with jobs or advantages is nepotism, so such help is described this way.

clue.text: Report of gun law

indicators.note: report means what is heard, so the word for the gun is spoken

parts.note: a cannon is a big gun

explanation.surface: The bang of a firearm and a mention of legislation.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a rule or law, especially church law.

clue.text: Interest in Eastern songs, reworked, Queen covered

indicators.note: covered says the rearranged letters cover the queen letter
reworked says the letters of songs are rearranged

parts.note: R is short for Regina, queen

explanation.surface: Eastern songs remixed and covered by the band Queen hold the attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reworked' turns SONGS into NGOSS, which wraps R.
explanation.definitionFit: To interest someone deeply is to absorb or engross them.

clue.text: Quiet before long surrounds northern river

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

indicators.note: surrounds says the soon word goes round the northern letter

parts.note: anon means soon, before long

explanation.surface: Calm descends before a long stretch around a northern river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' is part of 'before long', not a placing word. The Shannon is Ireland's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shannon is a river, the longest in Ireland.

clue.text: Speech is over before Budget

indicators.note: before places the over letter ahead of the budget word

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
a ration is a fixed allowance, a budget

explanation.surface: A political speech finishes ahead of the Budget announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: The Budget is the British government's annual statement of taxes and spending.
explanation.definitionFit: An oration is a formal speech, especially a ceremonial one.

clue.text: Commanding officer and male crew fix launch

parts.note: a crew is a body of men
to cement is to fix firmly

explanation.surface: An officer and his sailors prepare to launch a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Commencement is a beginning or start, which a launch is.
